newsitem.title: USA: CoreStates Q3 0.9 pct up on lower costs.
newsitem.headline: CoreStates Q3 0.9 pct up on lower costs.

text.p: CoreStates Financial Corp said third-quarter operating earnings rose 0.9 percent to $194.86 million with help from cost controls.

In a statement chairman and chief executive Terrence Larsen said while the bank had moderate revenue gains from the second quarter, revenue levels were virtually unchanged from a year ago while expenses were lower.

He said return on average assets was 1.79 percent in the the third quarter while return on aveage equity was 19.5 percent, ranking CoreStates among the best of the 50 largest U.S. banking companies on industry measures of profitability.

Larsen said CoreStates showed "steady progress with continued strong performance ratios as we continue working through the rapid integration of our largest merger ever." On April 9, CoreStates merged with Meridian Bancorp. Larsen said the bank is on track toward its goal of achieving one-fourth of a total $186 million in merger savings this year.

CoreStates said credit quality remained strong. Total non-performing assets were $264 million at September 30, compared to $254 million at June 30, and $321 million at September 30, 1995. The September 30, 1996, total represented 0.6 percent of total assets and 0.8 percent of total loans.
